archetypes.name: parity-drift
archetypes.rationale: A sh-to-py port of 13 verbs risks subtle behavioral divergence in fd-3 vs stdout routing, exit-code semantics, and value quoting that generic correctness checkers overlook.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the per-verb emitter routing table in the plan against `python/session_env.py` and every call site in the diff: verify each verb writes to the correct channel (fd-3 contract stream via `quiet_init`/`emit_kv`, plain stdout, EXIT-trap stdout, or silent file-only). Check that `read-key` emits the value only (no `KEY=` prefix) on fd-3, that `entry-gate` success KVs go to fd-3 under command-substitution capture, and that the four `read-key` default rules (A.6b present-but-empty included) are all present. Verify exit-code semantics: `persist-run-flags` and `write-run-params` must exit 2 on validation failure, `entry-gate` must exit 4, `write-id` failure must use the bash `FAILED=true`/`ERROR=` envelope split. Verify `write-design-env` uses `printf '%q'` (or equivalent) for source-safe quoting of all values and that the symlink stays under hardcoded `~/.cache/larch/sessions` even when `XDG_CACHE_HOME` is set. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: writer-guard
archetypes.rationale: The NEVER #14 writer-guard introduces a new runtime security boundary with three distinct path predicates and per-writer key allowlists whose correctness cannot be inferred from general security review alone.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the NEVER #14 writer-guard implementation in `python/session_env.py`: verify that the writer-target validator (predicate 2) and the broad cleanup predicate (predicate 1) are distinct code paths and that cleanup's broader allowlist is not reachable from session-content write paths. Check that the CR/LF byte rejection runs before any bytes are written and that it is applied to every value in every `write-*` verb. Confirm the per-writer key allowlists are explicit constants (not computed from input) and that unknown keys cause a hard rejection rather than a silent drop. Verify all three carve-outs: `/dev/null` bypasses the path allowlist, `--plugin-root-only` uses only value-grammar and parent-dir-writability validation (no session-tmpdir membership check), and the design-env symlink uses a dedicated validator permitting only the hardcoded `~/.cache/larch/sessions/current-design-env-$PPID.sh` location. Check that atomic writes (O_EXCL temp + os.replace) and symlink-target refusal are present for every session-content write path. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: module-boundary
archetypes.rationale: The plan explicitly forbids unifying cache-root helpers, local-cleanup implementations, and finalize import direction; violations would silently change ship/postmerge behavior and break parity harnesses.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that `session_env.py` and `finalize.py` each define their own `cache_sessions_root` / `cleanup_cache_sessions_root` implementation with the documented differing XDG semantics (finalize: absolute-XDG-else-`Path.home()/.cache`; session_env: bash-expansion-style `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-${HOME:-/tmp}/.cache}/larch/sessions`). Check that `finalize.py`'s `_local_cleanup` is untouched and that `local-cleanup` in `session_env.py` is an independent standalone port with no call into the finalize module. Verify that `restore_finalize_state_main` in `session_env.py` operates on exactly the 20-key allowlist from `lib-finalize-state-keys.sh` and has not been expanded with keys like `FORKED_TARGET` or `MERGE_RESULT`. Confirm the import direction: `session_env.py` may be imported by `finalize.py`, but `session_env.py` must not import `finalize.py` (no layering inversion). Check that the `read_finalize_state` and `write_finalize_state_merged` primitives moved from `finalize.py` are re-exported from `finalize.py` or imported back so existing consumers in `finalize.py` still work. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
